correctness.rationale: Full n>=4 proof follows Green (2008) integral homology and explicit clique classification. The punctured link is Cl(J(n,2)) with H2 basis of octahedral four-coordinate spheres; each is explicitly coned by a surviving even four-set. Mayer–Vietoris gives primitive short exact inclusion and no other punctured homology. Van Kampen, Hurewicz, high-dimensional elementary collapses, and the homology Whitehead theorem prove the actual integral three-sphere wedge. All boundaries n=4,5,6,7 rechecked by independent complete face enumeration and mod-two boundary ranks. No finite-to-infinite inference.

originality.rationale: Full-complex homology and clique classification are already Green 2008, explicitly attributed. This claim adds the all-dimensional *induced vertex deletion* homotopy type and a primitive split inclusion, requiring a nontrivial octahedral link-to-deletion calculation. The full-cube rational representation theorem Galetto–Montaño–Wellner 2026 does not imply this induced-deletion map. Targeted publication and indexed research-record searches for the exact object and aliases found no equivalent or dominating statement. Uninspected full text and unindexed sources remain residual originality risks.
residual_risks: The later portions of arXiv:2606.20784v1 were inaccessible; only the introduction, main theorem and overview material were read, so not claimed whole-document NOT_COVERING.
The full Green sequel arXiv:0812.1208 was not materially inspected beyond the abstract.
Unindexed publications, independent manuscripts or differently phrased robustness formulas may exist.

The recent motivating publication studies the full hypercube, while a foundational unpunctured half-cube theorem is from 2008; the claim is new only for the vertex-deleted space and associated inclusion.

value.rationale: The natural single-point loss problem on symmetric Hamming parity samples asks for exact robustness of homotopy, not just an ambient Betti table. For every n>=4 it yields the complete integral homotopy type and primitive inclusion with a nontrivial cubic rank deficit, including destruction of the entire sphere at n=4. This precise effect is not entailed by Green’s ambient homology or full-cube rational representations; the four-coordinate cone mechanism is structural and can guide multi-point investigations.
